August 26 recap: Northwest Indiana news you may have missed today
Don't miss Wednesday's most popular stories from The Times.
(9) updates to this series since
Michigan City schools renewed agreements with Sodexo and Safe Harbor, covering facilities management and after-school services.
Lake Central school officials say the district was “very fortunate” compared to others despite losing power to every building after the Aug. 11 derecho.
Sebastian Bach is joining Twisted Sister founding members Jay Jay French and Eddie Ojeda for an October concert at Hard Rock Casino.
Protests against companies are rare in Northwest Indiana, but NIPSCO will face its third round of protests since March — this time after lengthy power outages following recent storms.
Painter Jane Cowley uses layered color and nuanced light to capture portraits, landscapes and still lifes in a new exhibition at the Depot Museum and Art Gallery in Beverly Shores.
Reapers Realm terrified haunted-house fans for more than three decades. Now Hammond is demolishing the century-old building and looking to red…
Hammond has been demolishing the gabled building that was originally an office for Joseph Meyer's herb business and that ended up as Northwest Indiana's most popular haunted house.
The Chicago Bears got a slew of positive injury updates at their final Halas Hall training camp practice of the summer.
A Gary man faces arson and vandalism charges after police found a donation bin filled with clothes and shoes engulfed in flames.
SerenDIPity Ice Cream Shop in downtown Griffith lost all its ice cream and food during the tornado that swept through in June, which left its freezer on the fritz.
